newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Shares in some Yieh Loong affiliates slump.
newsitem.headline: Shares in some Yieh Loong affiliates slump.

text.p: Shares in some firms affiliated with Taiwan's Yieh Loong steelmaking group slumped on Wednesday amid renewed official allegations of financial fraud.
Shares of Yieh Phui, Yieh Loong, Yieh-Hsing and Ornatube Enterprise all fell the daily seven percent limit amid media coverage of the renewed allegations.
The four companies, in similarly worded statements, repeated their earlier denials of the allegations.
"Absolutely, we have no fake invoices or fake trade among the group member companies," the firms said.

Prosecutor Lin Ying-hua said investigators and police on Tuesday launched new checks of the group's member companies as they suspected the group of involvement in making fake invoices worth over T$20 billion that were fraudulently used by 12 companies to obtain bank loans or help their listings.
Lin told state television the alleged scam involved repeated sales between group affiliates of "millions of kilograms" of an unspecified commodity.
Prosecutors and police carried out a similar probe of Yieh Loong members in October, but no results were announced.
The group strongly denied any wrongdoing at that time.
The four firms produce a variety of specialised steel products.
